Concept 1.name: Urgency and Responsibility
Concept 1.definition: This group highlights the pressing need for immediate action on climate change while addressing the responsibilities felt by current and future generations. It emphasizes the importance of fostering hope and engagement in environmental issues.

Cluster 1.name: Climate Change Urgency
chunks: It's been in the back of my mind for quite a while, the whole climate change debate, environmental issues, growing pollution. So I've always felt very strongly about it and I've been watching very carefully what others have been doing. And for me, over the last few years, the urgency and the positivity, particularly the positivity around the debate has been missing. It's been very negative. Understandably, it's such a large issue that everyone feels completely overwhelmed by the facts, the scale of the problems and things like that.

We all get that there's a really big urgent message. And I'm not saying we shouldn't talk about the urgency or the big issues, but ultimately if we want to tackle this, if we want to get on the front foot we've got to bring people with us and people have got to feel like there's hope, there's a chance we can fix this.

Cluster 4.name: Future Focus
chunks: We've got 10 years of critical time where we have to be making inroads and finding these solutions and inspiring people that we can fix these solutions. Because past 2030, things get rapidly worse very quickly.

But it shouldn't be that there's a third generation now coming along having to ramp it up even more. And for me, it'll be an absolute disaster if George is sat here talking to you or your successor, Adam, in another 30 years time, whatever, still saying the same thing, because by then we'll be too late.

Cluster 9.name: Generational Responsibility
chunks: And I feel bad, I don't want to give them the burden of that worry.

I think it's been a hard road for him. My grandfather started off helping out WWF a long time ago with its nature work and biodiversity. And I think that my father progressed that on and talked about climate change and lot more, very early on before anyone else thought it was a topic.

Concept 2.name: Community Engagement and Nature Connection
Concept 2.definition: This concept emphasizes the importance of community involvement in environmental conservation and the intrinsic connection between individuals, particularly children, and nature. It highlights the role of local stewardship in fostering environmental responsibility.

Cluster 2.name: Community Conservation
chunks: I love community conservation and Namibia have been some of the world leaders in community conservation. For people who don't know what that is, it's effectively the locals, wherever you are in the world, taking an interest and management of the wildlife nature, the environmental assets around them. So they very much manage them. They protect them, they nurture them for their own prosperity.

Cluster 10.name: Nature Connection
chunks: They love it, children love being outdoors. They love getting muddy. They love playing and then chasing and playing sport and all that stuff. And I think they have a truer appreciation of what we're going to miss and what we're letting down own than actually many of the adults.

Concept 3.name: Innovation and Awareness
Concept 3.definition: This group focuses on the pursuit of innovative solutions to environmental challenges and the critical role of education and awareness in fostering a proactive approach to sustainability. It underscores the importance of technological optimism and community understanding.

Cluster 3.name: Earthshot Prize Goals
chunks: And that's what the Earthshot Prize is about, is providing those solutions to some of the world's biggest environmental problems.
Well, I think it should go Earthshot, BAFTA's, Oscar's, but hey, it depends-
So the original genesis of this is to try to capture the ingenuity and the problem solving and the ambition of the Moonshot.

Cluster 5.name: Technological Optimism
chunks: Absolutely, Adam. So that is the key, is it's about inspiring and finding solutions that can be around us right now and hopefully in the future. Rather than just the debate, concentrating on what we need to give up, what we can't do, which is very negative.
And it's not just about technology, as you pointed out. The Earthshot Prize isn't just about technology. There are plenty of technological solutions we can celebrate.

Cluster 11.name: Environmental Solutions
chunks: We need heroes. We need those people who really have got vision, who've got ambition, energy to step up, come forwards and give us solutions.
It's about thinking outside the box. It's about doing stuff in a different way that makes us richer, healthier and happier in the future.

Cluster 7.name: Environmental Awareness
chunks: I think a definite sense of realization and understanding. So the education piece is really key. So, for instance, not overusing water, being careful with our resources, turning off light switches. Things like that, which was instilled in me growing up.
But I think it is slowly dawning on them that these things matter.

Cluster 12.name: Space vs Earth
chunks: We need to be focusing on this one rather than giving up and heading out into space to try and think of solutions for the future.
That is also, yeah, a fundamental question.
